summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 10.1% YoY to INR1,717 crore and EBITDA fell 43% to INR131.5 crore, hit by LPG and truck disruptions and rupee depreciation.
summary.overview: PG Electroplast's Q4 FY26 was hurt by an LPG shortage in March that cut RAC production at Supa, a truck shortage that deferred dispatches, and about 20% rupee depreciation against the dollar. Management estimated roughly INR420 crore of revenue loss in the quarter and a PBT impact of about INR120 crore. Full-year revenue rose to INR5,288 crore but PAT fell to INR193.6 crore from INR290.9 crore. Management said channel inventory has normalised after April and May sell-out, and guided FY27 to better-than-industry growth with EBITDA margin recovering towards 8%, while declining to give a numeric FY27 revenue or PAT number.

segments.name: Room AC (RAC)
segments.commentary: Q4 RAC revenue INR1,210 crore, down 12% YoY; full-year RAC revenue grew 9%. Management said FY26 AC sales in December quarter were about INR932 crore vs INR516 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Washing machines
segments.commentary: Grew 52% for full FY26 and about 70% in Q4. Management targets 30-35% growth in FY27, with specifics to be given after Q1.

segments.name: Coolers

segments.name: Goodworth Electronics (JV)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR155.1 crore vs INR107.6 crore YoY; EBITDA INR6.19 crore vs INR0.94 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth targeted to be better than industry growth; no numeric revenue guidance given.
EBITDA margin expected to improve towards 8% in FY27 as operating leverage returns and input costs moderate.
Management said PBT should move broadly in line with sales growth, provided the rupee does not move beyond about INR97/USD; it sees FY27 PAT crossing FY25 levels if conditions normalise.
Working capital intensity expected to improve; operating and free cash flow expected to improve in FY27.
Total inventory targeted to fall from about INR1,601 crore at end-March to below INR900 crore by June-end 2026.
PLI incentive for FY26 of INR71 crore (including NGM PLI) to be received and recognised in FY27, versus INR37.5 crore currently and INR50 crore for the next year as stated on the call.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of INR785 crore, of which nearly INR500 crore went to land and buildings (Greater Noida 10-acre washing machine campus, Sri City 50-acre campus, Supa compressor building, 72-acre Kamargaon land in Ahmednagar, 8-acre Salarpur campus); RAC plant and machinery about INR165 crore; washing machine plant about INR70 crore.
Refrigerant manufacturing plant in Sri City: commercial production targeted by Q4 FY27, meaningful revenue in FY28, tie-up with an anchor customer in place.

Rotary compressor plant at Supa: machinery ordered, installation from August 2026, operations by Q4 FY27; 2 million compressors in phase 1, expandable to 4 million in phase 2. About 60% localised value-add. Management said no external approval or JV is needed. Full capacity targeted in FY28.
Expanded washing machine facility at Greater Noida is operational. Molding consolidation at Salarpur, Rajasthan to be ready around July-August 2026.

Expected FY27 capex of about INR400 crore. Management targets 4x asset turn by 2029. Average AC utilisation in FY26 about 45-50% on about 4.5 million annual capacity; FY26 production about 1.75 million sets plus 0.25-0.3 million extra IDUs.
demand_pricing: RAC industry declined about 15% in FY26 due to a delayed monsoon, the GST rate-cut announcement in August, and BEE-rating pull-forward into December 2025. Industry manufacturing in FY26 estimated at 13-14 million units.

Channel inventory peaked at about 5 million units in FY26 and management says it is now normalised. April and May sell-out was better than last year; management said it will not forecast FY27 volumes until about July.

Price hikes of about 10-15% industry-wide from December 2025 to April 2026; PG Electroplast took about 10-12% cumulatively, with a further increase in June quarter. Rupee moved from about INR93 to INR95.5 per dollar; management says exchange-rate movement is the main unpassed cost.
Management said FY26 industry-wide weakness was similar to FY23 and that no top-client-specific deterioration occurred. Top 3 client mix unchanged.
El Nino is forecast to intensify from July with a peak in September, which management said could extend the AC season. RAC penetration is below 10% of households.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins contract, and did the inventory bought cheaply in December and January help?
qa_highlights.answer: Most cheap inventory was consumed by the December quarter sales of about INR932 crore (vs INR516 crore). Price increases in January-March did not fully pass through rupee depreciation or commodity costs. LPG switchover energy costs were also absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the price hike was passed on, and how will gross margins normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10-12% price increase taken cumulatively. Gross margin % in AC will stay lower in FY27, but gross contribution per piece should return to historical averages.

qa_highlights.question: How much forex loss is in the numbers and where does it sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex loss sits in other expenses. Unhedged LC and payables were marked to INR94.8 at March-end, and the rupee has since moved to INR95.5. Hedging of $15-20 million was done around INR93.

qa_highlights.question: Will you give FY27 volume or revenue numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance. Management expects FY27 AC numbers to be much better than FY26 from a low base, and will firm up views after Q1 and around mid-July.

qa_highlights.question: Is the compressor project subject to approvals, and is there a Chinese partner?
qa_highlights.answer: No approval is needed and there is no JV; the company is going on its own, having acquired the technical capability. Customer tie-up and product approval are in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What was the capex breakup and asset turn?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex INR785 crore, of which about INR500 crore land and buildings. FY27 capex about INR400 crore; 4x asset turn targeted by 2029.

qa_highlights.question: Where does inventory stand and how much will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was about INR1,601 crore at March-end (AC INR1,300 crore, of which finished goods about INR450 crore; others INR300 crore). Target is below INR900 crore by June-end.

risks_watch: Rupee depreciation beyond the INR97/USD assumption, and continued aluminium and copper inflation, could erode the margin recovery and widen forex losses.
Q1 FY27 RAC sell-out, especially June, depends on monsoon timing; management will not give volume numbers before mid-July.
Execution of the Sri City refrigerator and Supa compressor plants by Q4 FY27, and the FY28 utilisation targets (about 50-55% for refrigerators, over 70% for compressors).
Working capital: inventory reduction to below INR900 crore by June-end and the timing of PLI receipts (INR71 crore for FY26, expected in FY27).
Labour availability, LPG supply and truck availability, which caused the March disruption and could recur.
Mentioned tension from the final PLI target year, which management said could push some industry players to aggressive volumes.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term numbers and explicit about refusing to give FY27 volume or revenue guidance, but confident that channel inventory has normalised and that margins will recover. Management attributed the decline mainly to external shocks: LPG, trucks, the rupee and weather.
key_quotes: So had these sales happened, we would have actually crossed INR2,100 crores plus in sales.
Channel inventory have now normalized materially from the peak of approximately 5 million units seen during FY26.
We expect EBITDA margins to improve towards 8% as operating leverage returns, input cost pressures moderate and our cost discipline initiatives take effect.
The problem is the exchange rate. Exchange rate is something which is so volatile in moving.
